children: Elmet signed a long-term tungsten concentrate offtake agreement with Tungsten West covering production from the Hemerdon Mine in Devon, England.
The critical materials provider expects to take more than 1,000 metric tonnes per year of tungsten concentrate from Hemerdon, with both parties aiming to increase production volumes over time.
Material will be converted into ammonium paratungstate and downstream tungsten intermediates through Elmet's allied refining network.
That will be followed by delivery to Elmet's U.S. manufacturing operations in Maine, Michigan, Ohio and Germany, pending the closing of another purchase agreement.

The partnership comes after the U.K. government invested in Tungsten West in August, while the U.S. government invested $450 million in Elmet earlier this month. Elmet established a new division following the investment from the Pentagon, which will focus on securing access to critical materials.
The Hemerdon mine is targeting ramp-up to full-scale production by the end of the first quarter.
